subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If the letters of the word EAMCET are permuted in all possible ways and the words thus formed are arranged in dictionary order, then find the rank of the word EAMCET.

mark_split.label: Write the letters in alphabetical order
Count the words that come before
Add up and state the rank

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the dictionary rank of EAMCET — what you write first, how you count the words before it, and how you finish.
insider_note: The two E letters make this the different one among the rank questions: the A and C blocks are 5!/2! = 60 each, not 120. Miss that division and every later number moves — the marks are in the block table, not the final addition.

steps.label: Alphabetical order of the letters
steps.margin_note: First mark. Six letters with E repeated twice: A, C, E, E, M, T. The repeat matters — blocks that still contain both E letters are divided by 2!.
lines: Letters of EAMCET in alphabetical order:
A, C, E, E, M, T (E occurs twice)

recall.must_convey: That the letters of EAMCET are first written in alphabetical order, noting the repeated letter: A C E E M T.
accept: write the letters in alphabetical order A C E E M T
first arrange the letters of EAMCET alphabetically
alphabetical order of the letters is A C E E M T
letters ni alphabetical order lo rayali, A C E E M T
sort the letters first, that is what dictionary order means
heard_as: A C E E M T

steps.why: Dictionary order is alphabetical order applied letter by letter. Until the letters are sorted there is no way to say which words come before the given one.
common_mistakes: Listing E only once — EAMCET has two E letters and the count of arrangements depends on it.
Writing the letters in the order of the word instead of alphabetical order.

steps.label: Count the words before it
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Words starting with A or C still contain both E letters, so each block is 5!/2! = 60. With E fixed, E A C and E A E give 3! each. After E A M the remaining letters C, E, T are already in order, so EAMCET is the next word.
lines: After EAM, the letters C, E, T are in order,
so the next word is EAMCET itself.

recall.must_convey: That words starting with A and with C are 5! over 2! = 60 each because of the repeated E, then E A C and E A E are 3! each, and after E A M the next word is EAMCET.
accept: A block sixty, C block sixty because of the two E letters, then EAC six and EAE six, then EAMCET
five factorial by two factorial for A and for C, three factorial for EAC and EAE, then the word
divide by two factorial for the repeated E in the first two blocks, then six and six
A tho C tho five factorial by two factorial sixty, EAC EAE three factorial, tharvatha EAMCET
sixty plus sixty plus six plus six before EAMCET

steps.why: Every word that starts with a smaller letter comes before the given word, and once the first letter matches the same argument repeats on the second letter. Each line fixes one more letter and counts the arrangements of the rest.
common_mistakes: Counting the A block as 5! = 120 — the two E letters are alike, so it is 5!/2! = 60.
Adding a block for E A E after E A C without noticing both E letters are then used up — the E A E block is 3! because C, M, T remain.
Adding a block for E A M C — after E A M C the letters E, T are in order and EAMCET is the first.

steps.label: Add up and state the rank
steps.margin_note: Last mark. 60 + 60 + 6 + 6 = 132 words come before EAMCET, so its rank is 133.

recall.must_convey: That the counts are added and one is added for the word itself, giving rank 133.
accept: add sixty, sixty, six, six and one to get one hundred thirty three
the rank is one thirty three
one hundred thirty two words come before it so the rank is one thirty three
anni add chesi plus one cheste one hundred thirty three
sixty plus sixty plus six plus six plus one is one thirty three

steps.why: The rank is the position of the word, so it is the number of words before it plus one for the word itself. Forgetting the plus one gives the count of earlier words, not the rank.
common_mistakes: Answering 132 — the count of words before EAMCET, not its rank.
Using 120 instead of 60 for the first two blocks and reaching 253.
